newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel delays hearings on CIA nominee.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel delays hearings on CIA nominee.

text.p: The head of the Senate Intelligence Committee postponed Tuesday for the second time confirmation hearings for Anthony Lake, President Clinton's nominee to become the next director of central intelligence.

Chairman Richard Shelby, an Alabama Republican, said that, "based on the many unanswered, perplexing questions that remain" about Lake, his panel would delay hearings until March 11. The sessions initially had been postponed until the week of Feb. 25.
In a statement, Shelby said he was dissatisfied with the Justice Department, which ended two investigations on Friday that had been hurdles to Lake's confirmation.

Lake, Clinton's national security adviser during his first administration, agreed on Friday to pay $5,000 to settle a civil inquiry into whether his failure to promptly sell energy stocks violated federal conflict-of-interest laws.

The Justice Department on the same day announced it had found "no basis for any criminal charges" against Lake arising from testimony he gave in September about the administration's policy of turning a blind eye to Iranian arms shipments to Bosnian Muslims in 1994.
"While the Justice Department's report issued last Friday will certainly be considered, it raises as many questions as it purported to answer, and was as satisfactory as I had hoped," Shelby said.
